title: I'm hosting the second IRL AI Game Dev meetup in Toronto! Comment or DM for Luma link
author: MunchyCerealGuy
selftext:
I hosted some of y'all this past week (past event [here](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1wnfko4/im_hosting_an_irl_ai_game_dev_meetup_in_toronto/)) and it was really fun to be around people seriously invested in making games with AI or building tooling to support their AI game development. I'll be hosting the second meetup 3 weeks from now in Toronto and would love to see anyone from Toronto there.

This is a meetup for AI game devs who are actively using AI tools and agentic workflows to build games. It will be a cross between a meetup and a demo event (food and drink will be served). The event can provide a stage to present your game, share your experiences building agents for game dev/design, or share the role(s) agents play in what you're building.

If you're looking to advance the game development and design abilities of agents beyond what's currently on the market, this will be a place to learn a new tool, connect with others who have similar skills, and possibly create new opportunities.

Please comment below so I can share the link to register or you can DM me directly

See you soon!!

comments.author: KevinDL
comments.body:
Please don't take this the wrong way, but I genuinely think creating AI-exclusive game development meetups is a step in the wrong direction.

AI already has a significant perception problem within the game development industry. Creating separate communities specifically around AI-driven development only reinforces the idea that AI developers exist in some entirely different category from everyone else. That won't help broader adoption or acceptance. If anything, I think it risks widening the divide.

We already have game development meetups, networking events, and communities where developers share tools, workflows, technical challenges, and projects. Why not participate in those? Bring your AI workflows, show what you've built, and talk with developers who might not otherwise engage with these tools. That's how you build understanding, challenge misconceptions, and potentially change opinions.

It also feels fundamentally backwards to organize a game development event around the tools rather than the games themselves. Nobody needs a separate meetup for developers who use Visual Studio, Blender, or procedural generation. Those are simply tools people use to make games. AI should ultimately be treated the same way.

If the goal is to advance AI adoption in game development, isolating AI enthusiasts into their own communities seems counterproductive. You're largely preaching to people who are already convinced rather than engaging with the broader industry.

I understand the appeal of meeting people who share your interests, and there's nothing inherently wrong with that. But I think we should be working toward making AI-assisted development a normal part of the broader game development conversation, not building an entirely separate identity around it.

And frankly, from an optics standpoint, this kind of thing comes across as a little cringe, which isn't helping AI's reputation right now.
